extracted.intended_audience: writers, poets, and artists considering submitting work to Black Fox Literary Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and sending fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, art, and blog submissions to Black Fox Literary Magazine (using their Submittable portal), including formatting, eligibility, rights, fees, and response times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication schedule and submission periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Two biannual issues (summer and winter) with specific open submission windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summer (2026) Issue Submission Period: January 1, 2026 – May 31, 2026. Winter (2027) Issue Submission Period: July 1, 2026 – November 30, 2026. Submissions received after the last day of the submission period will not be considered for that issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories accepted (what to submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Black Fox accepts fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry, art (cover art), blog posts, and contest entries; multiple submission service options are offered year-round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They accept general submissions in fiction, nonfiction, and poetry for each issue; also accept Submission with Donation, Expedited Response (4 or 2 weeks), Submission with Feedback (fiction & poetry), Art, Blog Posts, Cover Art, and contest entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single active submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit only one submission per submission period and have only one active submission at a time across categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send only one submission per submission period. Admin clarifies: submit only one submission across all categories at a time (i.e., if you have an open submission, do not submit another until that decision is made). Exceptions: paid services or contests may be handled differently; contest submissions may be allowed even if you've submitted for the period (see contest Q&A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method — Submittable only; no email
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be sent online through the journal's submission manager (Submittable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We only accept online submissions via our submission manager. We DO NOT accept submissions by email. If submissions are sent via email they will be automatically discarded without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submissions are accepted, but authors must promptly withdraw if the work is accepted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We accept simultaneous submissions, but we ask that you withdraw your work via Submittable (add a note if withdrawing one poem at a time) if your work is accepted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously published work policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously published pieces are not accepted; any portion posted online counts as previously published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We do not accept previously published pieces. This includes anything posted online. Any portion of work you’ve published online is considered previously published (the excerpt is considered published, not whatever piece the excerpt belongs to).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction/short fiction word-count limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Short fiction submissions must be 5,000 words or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep submissions to 5,000 words or less. The 5,000-word limit is a hard cutoff and is kept to keep things fair and mindful of pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose manuscript formatting (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting requirements for prose submissions: double-spaced, Times New Roman 12pt, author name and page number in top right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please make sure your manuscript is double-spaced with 12 point font (Times New Roman). Author’s name and page number should appear in the top right hand corner of every page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry submission quantity and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits and formatting specific to poetry submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please send only three poems at a time in one document. Poems do not have to be double spaced, but poets should still use Times New Roman, 12 pt. font and the poet’s last name/page number should still appear in the top right hand corner of every page. Keep in mind issue pages are 6×9; poems with particularly long lines often don’t work well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative nonfiction (personal essays and other creative nonfiction) is accepted with the usual manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We’re looking for personal essays and other creative nonfiction. There is no submission fee, but please prepare your manuscript according to our guidelines and submit through Submittable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flash fiction and flash nonfiction handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on submitting very short work and category placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For flash fiction: you may send two pieces of flash fiction in one submission. Flash nonfiction should be submitted under the nonfiction category regardless of length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art/cover art submission preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferences for art submissions intended for covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We prefer art that can be displayed on our cover in portrait format. Please do not send more than five pieces of art at a time. If submitting multiple pieces, we prefer images to be in one document. Review previous issues to get a feel for our tastes. Send your best artwork, including drawings, photographs, etc., through our submission manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs / image limitations (conflicting guidance noted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicting guidance appears: art submissions may include photographs for cover consideration, but elsewhere the magazine says it cannot consider photographs for the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier admin answers: 'we do accept photography under our Art submissions' and 'if you have a photograph you think meets our cover aesthetic, please feel free to submit.' Later admin: 'We are not able to consider photographs for our issue.' Because of the conflict, confirm current policy before submitting photos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine does not publish translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We do not publish translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter requirements for contests
rubrics_metrics.description: What to include in contest cover letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contest submissions: include a cover letter and state the genre as fiction, nonfiction, or poetry (they mean submission category). There are no other specific cover letter requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contests, fees, and refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Contest entry rules and fee policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summer writing contest is open to poetry, nonfiction, and fiction. Reading and contest fees are nonrefundable. The first-place winner of the biannual writing prize (fall and winter) receives $325; winners of the biannual Fox Tales Contest series (spring and summer) receive $300. Reading/contest fees are nonrefundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment to contributors and contributors copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation details for accepted contributors and cover artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of August 2023, Black Fox will pay each contributor of our issues $20 each. They are not able to supply contributor copies at this time; all issues are available on their website for free. Admin later states they have been paying $30 for cover art and that artists are compensated for their contribution. All payments made via PayPal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights policy and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights retained and obligations after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black Fox holds first North American serial rights for 60 days after publication. Authors agree not to publish, or authorize publication of any part of the material for 60 days following first publication. Should an author’s work be reprinted elsewhere after the 60-day period, Black Fox asks to be given credit as the first publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected time to decision and when to inquire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They aim for a 3–4 month response time. Authors may inquire if they haven’t heard in 6 months. Expedited response paid categories guarantee decisions in the timeframe selected (2- or 4-week options).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback/expedited submission service notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional paid submission services exist (expedited response, submission with feedback), but turnaround and availability can vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They offer Submission with Expedited Response (4 Weeks or 2 Weeks) and Submission with Feedback (fiction and poetry). The 'Submission with Feedback' option has no set turnaround time currently; availability may change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility notes (age, geography, content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of international and younger writers; content notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They accept submissions from anywhere in the world and have published high school writers in the past. Regarding sexual content: admin notes they cannot recall ever publishing explicit sex content—authors should review back issues to judge fit. They are interested in a wide variety of topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawals and Submittable procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: How to withdraw or correct submissions and account guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work is accepted elsewhere, withdraw it via Submittable (add a note if withdrawing one poem at a time). Submittable account technical issues should be resolved via Submittable support; a separate 'Black Fox' login is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on previously published excerpts
rubrics_metrics.description: An excerpt posted online counts as published; guidance on removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any portion of a work posted online is considered previously published. If you remove an excerpt from online, the remainder of the larger piece may then be considered for publication.
